newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japan finance minister says no bank crisis worries.
newsitem.headline: Japan finance minister says no bank crisis worries.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Saturday that even though Japanese banks were suffering from bad loan problems, there were no worries of a general banking crisis, Ministry of Finance (MOF) officials said.

Mitsuzuka, who is attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum's finance minister meeting here, made the comment in a meeting with Philippine President Fidel Ramos, Finance Minister Roberto de Ocampo and central bank governor Gabriel Singson.
"Japanese banks have some bad loans, but you should not worry about a crisis," Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying in the meeting, held ahead of the APEC ministers' session on Saturday.

He was referring to announcements last week by two of Japan's most troubled banks -- Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) and Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd -- of a merger with a healthier bank and a radical restructuring, the MOF officials said.
On Friday, NCB shares still remained weak, closing down 15 yen at 190, after brokers said the market was still unconvinced that its restructuring plan would be sufficient to revive it.
NCB, one of three long-term credit banks in Japan, announced it will write off bad loans totalling 460 billion yen, as well as sell off its Tokyo headquarters and withdraw from overseas operation.
Hokkaido Takushoku, one of Japan's top 20 city banks, also announced last week that it will withdraw from overseas operations and merge with a smaller regional bank.
